symbolic_mapping: elephant as enduring presence vs. aircraft as transient technology
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: The juxtaposition of massive organic form (elephant) with engineered flight apparatus (aircraft) evokes tension between biological persistence and human-made impermanence, prompting reflection on how artifacts mediate our relationship with time and mortality.
alternative_interpretations: This may simply reflect curatorial grouping by scale or thematic zone without symbolic intent.
limitations: No labels or contextual signage confirm intentional symbolism; arrangement could be logistical.

symbolic_mapping: display of life forms as curated knowledge
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: The organized presentation of diverse organisms under the explicit heading 'Life' frames biological reality as constructed knowledge, raising questions about how collective understanding shapes social existence through institutional curation.
alternative_interpretations: The banner may denote a temporary exhibition title rather than a philosophical statement.
limitations: The word 'Life' is isolated without accompanying explanatory text; its scope is ambiguous.

symbolic_mapping: vertical spatial hierarchy mirroring epistemic or social stratification
philosophy_interpretations.interpretation: Visitors occupy distinct vertical planes—ground floor, landing, balcony—suggesting implicit hierarchies of access or perspective within the institution, where position correlates with visibility and interpretive authority over displayed nature.
